Package com.github.crittscott.somegoogly.client

Class GooglyTracker.EyeInfo

java.lang.Object
com.github.crittscott.somegoogly.client.GooglyTracker.EyeInfo
Enclosing class:
GooglyTracker
public static class GooglyTracker.EyeInfo extends Object
Physics state for one pupil: its position and velocity in the eye's unit disk, the head orientation used to derive angular forcing, and the non-physical overlay values (grow/blink/tint) an active behavior writes each tick. update(net.minecraft.util.RandomSource, float, float, double, double, double, float, float, float) steps all of it by one tick.

    • gravX

      public float gravX
      World-down projected into this eye's pupil plane, in the (deltaX, deltaY) convention. Refreshed each render by GooglyEyeRenderer from the eye's animated world orientation, so the pupil sags toward true down; (0, -1), eye-local down, until the first render.

    • gravY

      public float gravY
      See gravX.

    • scaleMul

      public float scaleMul
      Non-physical behavior overlays, written each tick by the active behavior (neutral when none) and interpolated at render. Kept per eye so the blink mask varies by eye. This one is the grow scale; squashY is the blink, tintAmount the color-change blend, and tintColor the color-change target (set instantly, not interpolated).

  • Method Details

    • update

      public void update(net.minecraft.util.RandomSource rand, float headYaw, float headPitch, double motionX, double motionY, double motionZ, float anchorX, float anchorY, float stiffness)
      Advance the pupil simulation by one tick and update its previous/current render positions. Pupil positions and behavior anchors use the eye-local unit disk, with +X right and +Y up.
      Parameters:
      rand - randomness source (per-tracker / per-held-eye)
      headYaw - the holder's head yaw this tick (getYHeadRot)
      headPitch - the holder's pitch this tick (getXRot)
      motionX - the holder's X position delta this tick
      motionY - the holder's Y position delta this tick
      motionZ - the holder's Z position delta this tick
      anchorX - the behavior spring's X target in the unit disk (ignored when stiffness is nonpositive)
      anchorY - the behavior spring's Y target in the unit disk (ignored when stiffness is nonpositive)
      stiffness - positive behavior-spring strength; nonpositive values disable the spring
